rubric_intent: Score quickbox repo on engineering qualities: tests, code quality, and error handling.

dimensions.name: Test Suite Depth
dimensions.description: Measures whether tests actually exercise the core API across normal, edge, and error paths — not just smoke tests.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Look in tests/ or test_*.py. Count test files and test functions. Check whether tests cover edge cases (empty inputs, type mismatches, attribute errors on Box) vs. only happy-path. Run `pytest --collect-only` to enumerate. Compare README's '100% coverage' claim against actual test count and assertion density.

dimensions.name: Coverage Verifiability
dimensions.description: Measures whether the '100% test coverage' claim is substantiated by configuration and reproducible measurement.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Look for coverage config in pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, .coveragerc, or tox.ini. Check for a coverage CI step or badge. Run `pytest --cov` if available. If the claim is asserted in README but no coverage tooling exists, that is a strong negative signal.

dimensions.name: Type Safety Rigor
dimensions.description: Measures whether mypy coverage is real: type annotations on public API, py.typed marker, and mypy configuration in strict mode.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Check for `py.typed` file in the package directory. Inspect pyproject.toml/mypy.ini for `[tool.mypy]` strict settings. Read the Box class definition — are parameters and returns annotated? Run `mypy --strict <pkg>` if possible.

dimensions.name: Error Handling Quality
dimensions.description: Measures whether error paths raise specific, structured exceptions with context — vs. bare exceptions, silent failures, or unhandled paths.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Grep the source for `raise`, `except`, custom exception classes. Check whether errors include structured context (the 'structured context' README claim). Look for bare `except:` or `except Exception: pass`. Verify error paths have corresponding tests (test_*error*, pytest.raises).

dimensions.name: Public API Documentation
dimensions.description: Measures whether every public function/class has a docstring as claimed, and whether docstrings describe args, returns, and raised exceptions.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Inspect each public symbol in the package's __init__.py exports. Check for docstrings on Box and any public methods. Look for Args/Returns/Raises sections or a consistent docstring style (Google, NumPy, Sphinx).

dimensions.name: Dependency Discipline
dimensions.description: Measures whether the 'zero dependencies' claim holds and whether dev dependencies are pinned and minimal.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Inspect pyproject.toml/setup.py `dependencies` and `install_requires`. Check for `requirements.txt`. Verify the runtime dep list is empty. Note whether dev/test deps are scoped under an extras_require or [tool.poetry.dev-dependencies] block.

dimensions.name: CI and Quality Gates
dimensions.description: Measures whether tests, type checks, and lints actually run on every commit via CI configuration.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Look for .github/workflows/, .circleci/, .gitlab-ci.yml, or tox.ini. Check that CI runs pytest, mypy, and a linter (ruff/flake8/black). Absence of CI in a repo claiming 'production-ready' is a strong negative signal.

dimensions.name: Code Cleanliness and Linting
dimensions.description: Measures adherence to a consistent style via configured linters/formatters and absence of dead code or TODOs in core paths.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Check pyproject.toml for ruff/black/isort/flake8 config. Run the configured linter. Grep source for TODO/FIXME/XXX. Inspect for unused imports or commented-out code blocks.
